title: Study Abroad Experience at the Medical University of Gdańsk
paragraphs: I was allowed to do clerkships for three months at the Medical University of Gdańsk in Poland. Starting from the visa application at the embassy, everything, such as life in a dormitory overseas, was new to me, but supported by many people, I was able to lead a very fulfilling study abroad life. The main reason I chose the Medical University of Gdansk as my destination was that I was very attracted by the various wonderful experiences that can never be had in Japan, which I heard about from a senior in my club who had studied abroad there before.

The official language is Polish, but the university has a course called the English Division, in which all conversation and classes are conducted in English. About 300 students are enrolled per year, and surprisingly about 70% of them are women. The students came from all over the world, including India, Iraq, Italy, Canada, Sweden, Spain, Saudi Arabia, Germany and Norway. By interacting with students with completely different backgrounds, I was stimulated by their attitude toward medicine and their clear vision for the future. I was also able to reconfirm that I myself am being allowed to study in a truly fortunate environment, and it became a very instructive three months.

In the clerkships, I joined a different group of fourth- and fifth-year students every one or two weeks and rotated through surgery, medical oncology, pediatrics, cardiac surgery, orthopedics and anesthesiology. Because the Academic Affairs staff sent me the schedule beforehand, I could check the content and freely choose the departments I was interested in. As in the clinical clerkships in Japan, I was allowed lectures, ward clerkships, outpatient observation, operation observation and ICU observation. At the Medical University of Gdansk students study medicine from the first year, and progression is so difficult that about 30% repeat a year each year, so the students' amount of knowledge was correspondingly astonishing. Also, unlike in Japan, more than half of the doctors even in surgery and orthopedics are women, and seeing women working on the front line, not only those raising children but also those of an age to have grandchildren, I felt respect as a woman myself.

Because I rotated through many surgical departments, I was able to observe many operations, and it was a very meaningful clerkship. The new operating building was completed just last year and has 30 operating rooms, and I felt that the instruments used were almost the same as in Japan. At this university students have a great many opportunities to actually learn procedures, and during operation observation I did urinary catheterization, tracheal intubation and laryngeal mask insertion together with the anesthesiologist. I too was allowed to do tracheal intubation for the first time during a pancreatic cancer operation. At first the insertion of the tube did not go well and I struggled, but the doctor taught me the knack carefully and I was able to do it. In this way, weekdays were always days of tense learning, but on weekends I went around Poland and European countries with 中村, who studied abroad with me, and it became a study abroad life with a good balance of mind and body.

And above all, I was looked after very much by Professor Wozniak, a professor of biochemistry, and his secretary Adam. From the first day I arrived in Gdansk, besides the administrative procedures of course, on weekends we went cycling and shopping together, and Adam also supported me mentally. During the Easter holiday I was treated at Professor Wozniak's home to Polish regional dishes made by his wife, and he also arranged an occasion to eat sushi with the professor's son and his wife and grandchild. Professor Wozniak and his wife welcomed us warmly as if we were their own daughters, and thanks to their constant careful concern, I was able to spend the three months safely without ever becoming homesick. I was also blessed with the chance, through the professor's planning, to give a presentation in English to Polish high school students on the relationship between green tea and longevity, which was a very valuable experience.

Right after arriving in the city of Gdansk, it was my first time living alone in a foreign land, and I worried about whether I could live properly from then on, and there were times when I felt down, but encouraging each other with 中村, we were somehow able to get through it together. During my study abroad I came into contact with the kindness of many people, and I feel that I learned many important things not only about medicine but also as a person and was able to grow in mind and body. I intend to make good use of what I learned through studying abroad in my life from now on, and continue to make efforts so that I can certainly become a good doctor and repay everyone.

Finally, I would like to take this opportunity to convey my heartfelt gratitude to everyone at the International Collaboration Office and the Frontier Association, starting with Dr. 粕谷 and Dr. 長谷川, who gave me this valuable opportunity, everyone at the Medical University of Gdansk, my seniors, and 中村. Thank you very much.
